title: Supabase Authentication
outcome: Integrate Supabase Auth into Next.js with correct browser/server clients, cookie/session behavior, sign-up/sign-in/sign-out, and protected routing.
artifact: Working TaskFlow authentication UI/session integration whose server-side checks are explicit and ready to hand tokens to NestJS.
labSteps: Configure project URLs/redirects and explain why local/preview/production values differ.
Create browser and server Supabase clients with the correct key exposure model.
Implement sign-up/sign-in and surface provider errors safely.
Render authenticated state on the server rather than trusting only client state.
Implement sign-out and prove protected routes recover to unauthenticated state.
Inspect the session/access token and prepare the boundary for NestJS verification without exposing service-role credentials.
failureModes: Using service-role key in browser code
Relying only on client-side route hiding
mastery: Can distinguish public and secret Supabase keys
Can prepare a verified API handoff
principles: Let Supabase Auth establish user identity while the application still owns TaskFlow authorization rules.
Keep service-role credentials off the browser and use public client credentials only for intended client operations.
Handle session restoration and expiration explicitly so UI state does not silently drift from server identity.
Verify authentication on the server for protected operations rather than trusting client-visible session state.
